label: Sard's Theorem
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 125 through 149 and builds one long argument. Critical values are thin, that thinness lets us dodge bad projection directions for embedding, retraction returns approximations to the manifold, and transverse preimages behave like submanifolds. Keep the whole chain in view from the first slide.

label: Sets of Measure Zero
notes: Measure zero is the chapter's word for thin enough to avoid. A subset is null when arbitrarily small total volume covers it. Stress the countable-cover-of-cubes definition and that countable unions of null sets stay null, since the proof of Sard repeatedly slices the critical set into countably many pieces.

label: Measure Zero on Manifolds
notes: To speak of null sets on a manifold without a metric, declare a set null when every chart image is null in Euclidean space. The key lemma is that smooth maps between equal-dimensional opens send null sets to null sets, so the definition does not depend on which charts we picked.

label: Critical and Regular Values
notes: A critical point is where the differential fails to be surjective; its image is a critical value. Everything else in the target is a regular value, including points missed entirely. Use the saddle u squared minus v squared: the origin is the only critical point and zero its single critical value, while nonzero levels stay clean.

label: Sard's Theorem
notes: State the theorem cleanly. For any smooth map the set of critical values has measure zero, so almost every value is regular. Emphasize the asymmetry: the critical point set can be large and complicated, yet the values it produces in the target remain negligible. This is the engine for everything that follows.

label: Proof Strata
notes: Walk the staged reduction. Pass to charts, then split the critical set. Where a first derivative survives, slice transversally; where the first k derivatives vanish but a later one survives, push into a hypersurface; where many derivatives vanish, Taylor's theorem forces tiny cubes into even tinier balls. Negative volume exponents close the estimate.

label: Regular Level Sets
notes: The regular value theorem is Sard's immediate payoff. If c is a regular value the preimage is an embedded submanifold whose codimension equals the dimension of the target. Because regular values are almost all values, generic level sets are automatically manifolds, which is why we tolerate the critical fiber being singular.

label: Whitney Embedding
notes: Whitney's theorem says every smooth n-manifold embeds in Euclidean space of dimension two n plus one and immerses in dimension two n. The mechanism is repeated projection: lower the ambient dimension one step at a time, each step choosing a direction outside a measure-zero bad set supplied by Sard.

label: Avoiding Bad Directions
notes: Make the projection step concrete. A projection keeps an embedding embedded only if its kernel avoids tangent directions, which would destroy the immersion, and secant directions, which would glue two points together. Both families are images of low-dimensional maps, so by Sard they miss almost every direction once the ambient dimension is high enough.

label: Whitney Approximation
notes: Continuous maps are homotopic to smooth ones, and a continuous map already smooth on a closed set can be approximated without disturbing it there. The proof for manifold targets has two moves: approximate inside an ambient Euclidean space, then retract back through a tubular neighborhood to land on the manifold.

label: Tubular Retraction
notes: The tubular neighborhood is what makes the second move legal. A smooth manifold sitting in Euclidean space has a neighborhood that retracts smoothly onto it along normal directions. The circle is the honest model: a nearby smooth curve stays inside the annulus, and normalizing radius back to one is the retraction.

label: Transversality
notes: Two submanifolds meet transversally when their tangent spaces together span the ambient tangent space at every shared point. The preimage theorem generalizes regular values: if a map is transverse to a submanifold, the preimage is a submanifold of the predicted codimension. Empty intersections count as transverse vacuously.

label: Genericity and Recap
notes: Transversality is generic and stable. Parametric transversality plus Sard shows almost every member of a family is transverse, and any map is homotopic to a transverse one. Close by retracing the chain: thin critical values, embedding by avoidance, approximation by retraction, and transverse preimages that behave like submanifolds.
